chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Asadi narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Barmaki narrated to us. He said: 'Abdullah ibn Ahmad al-Shami narrated to us. He said: Isma'il ibn al-Fadl al-Hashimi narrated to us. He said:

I asked Abu 'Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) about Musa ibn Imran (peace be upon him) - when he saw their ropes and their staffs, how did he sense fear in himself while Ibrahim (peace be upon him) did not sense it when he was placed in the catapult and thrown into the fire?

So he (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Ibrahim (peace be upon him), when he was placed in the catapult, was relying on the lights of the Proofs of God, Mighty and Majestic, that were in his loins; and Musa (peace be upon him) was not like that. Therefore, he sensed fear in himself while Ibrahim (peace be upon him) did not.

key_terms.أنوار حجج الله: Lights of God's Proofs - referring to the spiritual lights of the prophets and Imams in Ibrahim's lineage
key_terms.المنجنيق: Catapult/trebuchet - the device used to hurl Ibrahim into the fire
key_terms.خيفة: Fear, apprehension - a Quranic term (20:67) describing an inner sense of fear
key_terms.صلبه: His loins/progeny - referring to future descendants who would carry divine authority

ai.seo_question: Why did Prophet Musa feel fear but Prophet Ibrahim did not when facing danger?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) explains why Prophet Musa (AS) felt fear upon seeing the sorcerers' ropes and staffs (as mentioned in Quran 20:67) while Prophet Ibrahim (AS) remained fearless when catapulted into fire. The Imam teaches that Ibrahim drew strength from the divine lights of God's future Proofs (the Imams and prophets) that were in his loins, a spiritual distinction Musa did not share. This reflects the Shia theological concept of the pre-existing prophetic and Imamic light (nur) transmitted through the lineage of Ibrahim.
